newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs up $0.50-$2.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs up $0.50-$2.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Monday sold up $0.50-$1.00, instances $2.00 per cwt higher, amid strong pork prices and firm packer demand, livestock dealers said.

Demand was excellent on outlooks for substantial increased pork exports following news late last week that Tawain, a major pork supplier to Japan, suspended pork exports because of foot and mouth disease in its hog herd, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $47.50 to $48.50 in the country and $49.50 to $50.00 at plants, they said.

Illinois hogs sold up to $2.00 higher, compared with Friday, with $49.00 to $50.00 paid in the country and up to $51.00 at plants, dealers said. Gains were furthered by light marketings as producers slowed shipments in anticipation of higher prices, they said.
"The runs are not what they ought to be, but there are some hogs moving," one Illinois hog buyer said.
Indiana hogs sold up $1.00 at $47.50 to $48.50 in the country and $49.00 to $50.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $46.00 to $47.00 in the country and $48.00 to $49.00 at plants.
